questions.question_text: A firm notices that its monthly rejection rate has risen from 2% to 6% and then decides to find out the cause before taking any step. Which stage of the control process is this?
options: Analysing deviations after comparing actual output with the standard
Taking the corrective action to bring the output back on plan
Setting the standard of performance for the coming period
Measuring the actual performance of the production department

questions.question_text: Why is controlling described as a function that both looks back and looks forward?
options: It is performed by the same person who has framed the plans
It reviews past results but also sets the ground for the next plan
It is concerned with the past events and has no use for the future
It is performed only after planning has been fully abandoned

questions.question_text: A standard of "good customer relations" is difficult to control mainly because it is:
options: Qualitative and hard to measure precisely
Set at too high a level for the staff to achieve
Applicable only to the top level of management
Based on the past performance of the firm alone

questions.question_text: The standard daily output of a machine is 800 units with a permitted deviation of 5%. Which actual output needs the manager's attention under management by exception?
options: 780 units
820 units
750 units
840 units

questions.question_text: In the above case, which of the following actual outputs needs NO corrective action?
options: 770 units
755 units
750 units
745 units

questions.question_text: A restaurant checks the freshness of vegetables before the kitchen begins cooking. This is an example of:
options: Feedforward control, exercised before the operations begin
Concurrent control, exercised while the operations go on
Strategic control, exercised over the long-term plans
Feedback control, exercised after the operations are over

questions.question_text: A supervisor stands at an assembly line and corrects a worker's method as the product is being made. This is:
options: Feedforward control, as the correction is made before the activity
Feedback control, as the correction is made after the activity
Budgetary control, as the correction is made in the budget
Concurrent control, as the correction is made during the activity

questions.question_text: A company studies customer returns of last quarter to improve next quarter's design. This is mainly:
options: Feedforward control, as it corrects the inputs before use
Preventive control, as it stops the problems from arising
Feedback control, as it uses the results of the completed work
Concurrent control, as it corrects the work in progress

questions.question_text: A division has net profit of Rs 4,50,000 and capital employed of Rs 30,00,000. Its return on investment is:
A division earning 12% ROI is offered a project that yields 10%, which is above the firm's cost of capital. The divisional manager judged on ROI:
options: Must accept it, since every project above the cost of capital is good
Should accept it, since it will raise the ROI of the division
May reject it, as it lowers divisional ROI, though it benefits the firm
Must reject it, since the project is bound to be loss-making for the firm
questions.explanation: ROI can conflict with firm goals.

questions.question_text: Fixed costs are Rs 3,00,000, the selling price is Rs 150 per unit and the variable cost is Rs 90 per unit. The break-even quantity is:
options: 3,333 units
7,500 units
5,000 units
2,000 units

questions.question_text: With the data of the above question, the sales needed to earn a profit of Rs 1,20,000 are:
options: 2,000 units
9,000 units
5,000 units
7,000 units

questions.question_text: Actual sales are 8,000 units against a break-even of 5,000 units, at Rs 150 per unit. The margin of safety is:
Margin of safety as a percentage of actual sales for the above firm is:
A budget for the month shows sales Rs 12 lakh, but the actual sales are Rs 13.5 lakh. The sales variance is:
options: Rs 13.5 lakh favourable
Rs 1.5 lakh favourable
Rs 12 lakh adverse
Rs 1.5 lakh adverse

questions.question_text: Actual cost of materials is Rs 5.4 lakh against the budget of Rs 5 lakh. This is:
options: Rs 5.4 lakh adverse
Rs 5 lakh favourable
Rs 40,000 adverse
Rs 40,000 favourable

questions.question_text: A flexible budget is superior to a fixed budget for control because it:
options: Considers only the sales and ignores the costs of the firm
Restates the budget for the actual level of activity before comparison
Remains the same at all the levels of activity of the firm
Is prepared once a year and is never revised by the managers

questions.question_text: Budgeted variable cost is Rs 40 per unit and budgeted output 5,000 units. At an actual output of 6,000 units, the flexed variable cost budget is:
Under zero-based budgeting, a manager requesting funds for an existing activity must:
options: Justify the need for that activity from scratch for the new period
Show that it received funds in the last budget period
Wait for the top management to decide on the allotment
Add a fixed percentage to last year's allotment

questions.question_text: The cash budget of a firm shows an expected closing cash balance of Rs (50,000). This indicates that the firm:
options: Will need to arrange additional funds during the period
Will break even during the period
Will earn a profit during the period
Will have idle cash which should be invested

questions.question_text: Standard material cost per unit is Rs 200 (10 kg at Rs 20). For 1,000 units, actual usage was 10,500 kg at Rs 20 per kg. The material usage variance is:
options: Rs 10,000 adverse
Rs 10,000 favourable
Rs 1,05,000 adverse
Rs 5,000 adverse

questions.question_text: Standard price Rs 20 per kg; actual price Rs 22 per kg for 10,000 kg. The material price variance is:
options: Rs 20,000 favourable
Rs 20,000 adverse
Rs 2,20,000 adverse
Rs 22,000 adverse

questions.question_text: Standard wage rate is Rs 50 per hour and 2,000 hours are allowed. Actual hours 1,900 at Rs 50. The efficiency variance is:
options: Rs 95,000 favourable
Rs 5,000 adverse
Rs 1,00,000 favourable
Rs 5,000 favourable

questions.question_text: The overall cost variance is the sum of the price (rate) variance and the:
options: Usage (efficiency) variance
Margin of safety
Sales variance
Overhead absorption variance only

questions.question_text: An organisation applies "critical point control" because:
options: It is uneconomical to watch every activity, so key points are chosen
It must report on every single activity to the government
It has no standards of performance for the remaining activities
It wants to check every activity in the same detail every day

questions.question_text: A company monitors closely the 5% of suppliers who provide 80% of the purchase value. This applies:
options: Standard costing, in the manner of the variance review
Zero-based budgeting, in the manner of the budget review
Break-even analysis, in the manner of the cost review
Selective control, in the manner of ABC analysis

questions.question_text: A store classifies items as A, B and C by annual usage value. For tight control, the management should concentrate on:
options: B items, which are medium in both number and value
All items alike, regardless of their usage value
A items, which are few in number but high in value
C items, which are many in number but low in value

questions.question_text: Annual demand is 3,600 units, ordering cost is Rs 100 per order and carrying cost is Rs 8 per unit per year. EOQ is:
options: 300 units
150 units
450 units
600 units

questions.question_text: With an EOQ of 300 and annual demand of 3,600, the number of orders per year is:
Just-in-time inventory control reduces:
options: The ordering cost, but increases the stock levels
The carrying cost of inventory, but increases the dependency on the suppliers
The dependency on suppliers, but increases the carrying cost
Both the carrying cost and the quality of the materials

questions.question_text: A firm aiming for 3.4 defects per million opportunities is following:
options: Break-even analysis, through a study of the cost-volume link
Management audit, through an appraisal of the management
Six Sigma, through statistical control of the process variation
Zero-based budgeting, through a review of every cost item

questions.question_text: Kaizen differs from a one-time quality drive because it requires:
options: Replacement of the older employees by the younger employees
Continuous small improvements by all the employees
A single large improvement by the quality department
Inspection of the finished goods alone

questions.question_text: The balanced scorecard goes beyond traditional financial control by also looking at:
options: Taxes, interest and depreciation of the firm
Customers, internal processes, and learning and growth
Sales, purchases and stock of the firm
Raw materials, wages and overheads of the firm

questions.question_text: Which statement about internal audit is correct?
options: It is carried out by the staff of the organisation as a continuous check
It is carried out by an independent auditor appointed by the shareholders
It is compulsory for all firms under the Companies Act
It is concerned only with the preparation of the final accounts

questions.question_text: MIS helps in control mainly by:
options: Checking the attendance of the employees of the firm
Replacing the managers in taking the decisions of the firm
Storing only the accounting records of the earlier years
Giving timely information about deviations for corrective action

questions.question_text: A control system that gives the report two months after the event is weak mainly in terms of:
options: Economy
Flexibility
Timeliness
Objectivity

questions.question_text: A firm spends Rs 5 lakh on a control system that saves only Rs 3 lakh of losses. This violates the principle of:
options: Economy
Flexibility
Objectivity
Suitability

questions.question_text: Employees resist a new biometric monitoring system because they feel distrusted. This is a:
options: Behavioural limitation of control
Financial limitation of control
Technical limitation of control
Legal limitation of control

questions.question_text: Control cannot be fully effective in controlling external factors such as a change in government policy because:
options: They are not important to the performance of the firm
They are too small to be noticed by the managers of the firm
They are controlled by the employees of the firm
They lie outside the firm and cannot be influenced by it

questions.question_text: When the actual output of 960 units is below the standard of 1,000 because the machine was old, the best corrective action is:
options: Reduce the standard permanently without any study
Punish the operators of the machine
Repair or replace the machine
Ignore the shortfall as it is only 4%

questions.question_text: If the deviation is found to arise because the standard itself was unrealistic, the manager should:
options: Replace all the workers
Stop the production
Ignore the deviation
Revise the standard

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of bureaucratic control?
options: Employees monitoring their own work
Using market prices to judge the performance
Relying on shared values and the norms of the group
Following written rules and procedures for approving expenses

questions.question_text: Which control relies on the shared values and norms of the group?
options: Market control
Output control
Clan control
Bureaucratic control

questions.question_text: A manager rewards the division which achieves its targets and ignores how it was done. This is:
options: Input control
Output (results) control
Clan control
Behaviour control

questions.question_text: Current assets are Rs 9 lakh, inventory Rs 3 lakh and current liabilities Rs 4.5 lakh. The quick ratio is:
With the above data, the current ratio is:
A firm has debt of Rs 20 lakh and equity of Rs 10 lakh. Its debt-equity ratio is:
Cost of goods sold is Rs 12 lakh and the average inventory is Rs 2 lakh. The inventory turnover and holding period (360 days) are:
options: 2 times and 180 days
12 times and 30 days
6 times and 60 days
6 times and 30 days

questions.question_text: Credit sales are Rs 18 lakh and average debtors are Rs 3 lakh. The average collection period (360 days) is:
options: 90 days
30 days
120 days
60 days

questions.question_text: A firm's net profit margin falls from 10% to 8% while sales stay at Rs 50 lakh. The fall in net profit is:
options: Rs 4 lakh
Rs 2 lakh
Rs 1 lakh
Rs 0.5 lakh

questions.question_text: Which of the following would show that a control system is "objective"?
options: Performance is measured by the mood of the superior
Performance is judged on the personal opinion of the manager
Performance is measured against clear, verifiable standards
Standards differ from person to person

questions.question_text: The comparison of actual with the standard shows no variance at all. The manager should:
options: Take no action, as the performance matches the standard
Take drastic corrective action to improve the performance
Stop the activity, since there is nothing left to improve
Revise the standard at once, as it is now out of date

questions.question_text: A production manager reduces the standard time for a job after finding that the workers complete it in less time easily. This is an example of:
options: Staffing the department
Directing the workers
Setting plans for the next year
Reviewing the standards as a part of control

questions.question_text: Control through "management audit" evaluates:
options: Only the stock held in the godown
The overall effectiveness of the management performance
Only the arithmetical accuracy of the books
Only the payment of the taxes

questions.question_text: Which of the following best illustrates feedforward control in a hospital?
options: Sterilising the instruments before the operation
Monitoring the patient's vital signs during an operation
Auditing the bills at the year end
Studying the patient complaints after discharge

questions.question_text: A bank uses CCTV and supervisors during the working hours to prevent fraud at the counter. This is:
options: Strategic control
Feedforward control
Feedback control
Concurrent control

questions.question_text: Which statement distinguishes control from coordination?
options: Both are the same
Control is a function of the lowest level only
Control harmonises efforts; coordination compares results with standards
Control compares results with standards; coordination harmonises the efforts of the people

questions.question_text: Which is an important benefit of a good control system?
options: Better coordination of activities and improved motivation
Removal of the need for planning in the organisation
Complete removal of the external risks to the organisation
A guaranteed profit in every year of its working

questions.question_text: The main reason for the failure of a good control system in practice is:
options: Resistance by the people and weak commitment of the managers
Too few employees working in the organisation
Excessive profits earned by the organisation
Lack of plans in the organisation as a whole

questions.question_text: Actual sales growth is 4% against a target of 10%. The manager first studies the causes of the shortfall. This follows:
options: Marginal costing, with the study of contribution
Zero-based budgeting, with the review of expenses
Break-even analysis, with the study of fixed costs
Management by exception, with the diagnosis of causes

questions.question_text: Which statement about a budget as a control device is TRUE?
options: It is prepared after the end of the period it relates to
It is a record of the transactions already completed
It is concerned with the past performance of the firm alone
It is a standard against which actual performance is compared

questions.question_text: The tool that shows the schedule of project activities against time on a bar chart is the:
options: Break-even chart
Pie chart
Organisation chart
Gantt chart

questions.question_text: PERT is preferred to a Gantt chart for complex projects because it:
options: Shows the dependence between activities and the critical path
Is easier to draw than a bar chart for the small jobs
Shows only the cost aspects of the activities of a project
Can be prepared without any estimates of the time required

questions.question_text: In a PERT network, an activity has the optimistic time 4, the most likely time 7 and the pessimistic time 16 days. The expected time is:
options: 7 days
10 days
8 days
9 days

questions.question_text: An activity with positive slack in a project network:
options: Has no effect at all on the completion of the project
Lies on the critical path of the project network
Can be delayed by the slack period without delaying the project
Must be completed first among all the other activities

questions.question_text: Statistical quality control uses sampling because:
options: Inspection of all units is always easy
Samples always give a perfect picture of the lot
Inspecting every unit is costly or sometimes destructive
It is required by the law

questions.question_text: An acceptance sampling plan accepts a lot if defectives in the sample are:
options: Within the pre-fixed acceptance number
Zero in every case
Equal to the lot size
More than the pre-fixed number

questions.question_text: A control chart is used to:
options: Chart the flow of cash into and out of the firm over a period
List the stock held by the firm in the order of its value
Map the organisation structure and the reporting lines of a firm
Plot sample measurements against upper and lower limits over time

questions.question_text: A point lying outside the upper control limit on a control chart suggests that:
options: The sample size taken for the chart was too small
The process may be out of control and needs investigation
The process is in perfect control and needs no attention
The standards are not needed for the process any more

questions.question_text: Total productive maintenance and preventive maintenance are examples of:
options: Financial control of the machines
Feedback control of machines
Budgetary control of the machines
Feedforward control of machines

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a TRUE statement about the span of control and the degree of control?
options: A wide span always improves the quality of supervision
A narrow span always reduces the cost of management
A very wide span makes close supervision difficult
A narrow span makes managers less informed

questions.question_text: Corrective action for a recurring problem differs from a quick fix because it:
options: Removes the root cause so the deviation does not recur
Treats only the symptom of the deviation
Is taken before the deviation occurs
Is always cheaper than the quick fix

questions.question_text: Which is a likely sign of over-control in an organisation?
options: Employees taking more risks in the work they undertake
Employees innovating freely in the work they undertake
Employees showing high morale in the work they undertake
Employees avoiding initiative for fear of breaking the rules

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of effective control?
options: It is understood by the people who use it
It is rigid and unchanged in all the situations
It is economical to the firm that uses it
It is timely in showing the deviations

questions.question_text: A firm's gross profit ratio falls from 30% to 25% on sales of Rs 40 lakh. The fall in gross profit in rupees is:
options: Rs 2 lakh
Rs 5 lakh
Rs 1 lakh
Rs 10 lakh

questions.question_text: A firm sets a standard of 2% rejections but the actual is 1.5%. This variance is:
options: Zero, since both are small
Adverse, since the actual is not equal to the standard
Not measurable
Favourable, since the actual is better than the standard

questions.question_text: The performance appraisal of employees is a tool of control over:
options: Human resources
Financial resources
Physical assets
Material resources

questions.question_text: The aim of inventory control is to:
options: Place the orders once a year to save the ordering cost
Keep adequate stock at the lowest cost without stock-outs
Avoid purchases altogether so that there is no carrying cost
Hold the highest possible stock to avoid any shortage

questions.question_text: Safety stock is held to guard against:
options: A rise in the wages of the workers of the store
Uncertainty in demand and in the lead time of supply
A fall in the prices of the goods held in stock
A change in the rates of taxes on the goods

questions.question_text: The reorder level is computed as:
options: Average usage × EOQ
Maximum usage × maximum lead time
Minimum usage × minimum lead time
EOQ × lead time

questions.question_text: Daily usage is 50 units and the lead time is 6 days. With a safety stock of 100 units, the reorder level (on average usage) is:
options: 300 units
400 units
350 units
500 units

questions.question_text: A warehouse maintains a record of its stock receipts and issues for every item. This is:
options: JIT system
Periodic inventory system
Perpetual inventory system
ABC analysis

questions.question_text: Which cost is reduced by an increase in the order size?
options: Carrying cost per unit
Cost of insurance
Ordering cost per unit
Cost of obsolescence

questions.question_text: Which cost rises with an increase in the order size?
options: Ordering cost
Carrying cost
Cost of the setup
Cost of stockouts

questions.question_text: The EOQ is at the point where:
options: Ordering cost is zero
Carrying cost is zero
Ordering cost equals carrying cost
Total cost is the highest

questions.question_text: The Pareto principle (80:20) states that, typically, about:
options: 10% of the causes produce 90% of the effects
20% of the causes produce 80% of the effects
80% of the causes produce 20% of the effects
50% of the causes produce 50% of the effects

questions.question_text: A manager analyses the 20% of customers who give 80% of revenue. This is consistent with:
options: The unity of command
The scalar principle
The Pareto principle
The gang plank

questions.question_text: Quality circles help control by:
options: Replacing the managers by the committees of workers
Increasing the number of inspectors in the factory
Involving groups of workers in solving the quality problems
Reducing the autonomy of the workers on the shop floor

questions.question_text: "Poka-yoke" is a Japanese term for:
options: An accounting method
Mistake-proofing the process
A marketing technique
A pay system

questions.question_text: Benchmarking involves:
options: Comparing the budgets of the firm with its own forecasts
Comparing processes and performance with the best in the industry
Comparing the wages of its employees with the minimum wages
Comparing this year's profits with those of the last year

questions.question_text: A firm compares its delivery time with that of the industry leader and sets it as a target. This is:
options: Time study
Sampling
Zero-based budgeting
Benchmarking

questions.question_text: Business process re-engineering involves:
options: A reduction in the salaries of all the employees of the firm
A radical redesign of processes to get major gains in performance
Small, gradual changes in the existing processes of the firm
An increase in the number of levels in the hierarchy

questions.question_text: A fraud is detected because the cashier and the accountant are different persons. This shows:
options: The failure of the budgets as a tool of control
The importance of separating duties as a control
The need for more employees in the accounts section
The use of ratios as a tool of financial control

questions.question_text: A firm requires two signatories for every payment above Rs 1 lakh. This is an example of:
options: External control
Market control
Strategic control
Internal control

questions.question_text: The main purpose of an audit trail is to:
options: Raise the sales of the firm through better records
Allow transactions to be traced back to their source
Hide the errors made by the staff in the records
Reduce the taxes payable by the firm every year

questions.question_text: A key limitation of ratio analysis as a control tool is that it:
options: Rests on past data and may not show present conditions
Is too costly for any firm to compute from its accounts
Ignores the financial statements of the firm altogether
Needs no comparison with any standard to be meaningful

questions.question_text: Strategic control is concerned with:
options: The daily output of each worker on the shop floor
The attendance of the employees in a department
Whether the strategy is working and achieving long-term goals
The petty cash held by the cashier of the firm

questions.question_text: Which is a control device in the area of marketing?
options: Wage sheet prepared for the employees every month
Sales analysis and market share analysis of the firm
Cash flow statement prepared for the firm every year
Machine hour rate worked out for the factory machines

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a human-resource control tool?
options: Cost sheet
Cash budget
Break-even chart
Performance appraisal

questions.question_text: The most important condition for an effective control system is that:
options: Standards are clear, accepted and communicated to the people
The results of the control are not shared with anyone
Standards are never revised, whatever may be the change
Managers alone know the standards that are being used
